Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Collect - Animal Alliance 1.1 Gameplay: 1.1.1 Create an Animal Alliance to win 1.1.2 Card Abilities 1.1.3 Team Play 1.1.4 Scoring Collect - Animal Alliance 2-5 players 64 cards - 8 of each animal. Shuffle the cards and split into two decks, put within reach. This game can be played as a team, but each player will form their own row. Gameplay: Take a card from either deck and place it in your row. Create an Animal Alliance to win Four adjacent cards of the same animal species. or, with an Octopus card, three different pairs of animals. Cards in a pair need to be adjacent but each pair does not need to be adjacent. or, with a lion card, 7 cards of different animal species. Card Abilities Chameleon - Acts as Wild card to be used as any animal towards the winning condition. But if you have two chameleons in your row, they must both retreat to the bottom of a deck. Crab - Choose a card (in your line up or your competitors line) and move it however many spaces. This will help (or hinder) achieving the four-adjacent card win condition. Hermit crab - If you have a crab or chameleon in your row, when drawn, you can take a second turn. Crocodile - Choose a card from another player's row and return it to the bottom of either deck. Monkey - Swap your new monkey card for another player's card. Parrot - Choose a deck and guess which animal will be drawn from it next. If you're correct, it's yours. Lion - Winning condition, 7 different animals. Octopus - Winning condition, 3 different pairs of animals. Cards in a pair need to be adjacent but each pair do not need to be adjacent. Team Play You're free to help your teammate achieve the winning condition and you can both work together to stop the other team achieving an animal alliance first. Scoring Each round, the winning player will receive a Half Crown. Achieve 2 Half Crowns to win the match. If there are no Half Crowns remaining, the winning player receives the Full Crown and the immediate win. [Rating: 2/10] More of the same. It is unbelievable for me how a poor game like this can be published in 2025.

[Rating: 2.5/10] Jeu de collection avec extremement peu de choix et du take that. C'est rapide mais en mode spectateur.

[Rating: 3/10] A pretty boring card game. Draw a card, keep or return it, and activate a simple ability.   Mostly mean take that cards. Each card COULD be used to yourself, or against others, so it's just a super frustrating boring "bash the leader" game.  Some memory elements involved to a point where it becomes annoying. You SHOULD try to remember what's on the returned cards, so you can "guess the color" for extra bonuses if you happen to draw a parrot. Very annoying.

[Rating: 3/10] [b]02/11/26[/b] - Cute little set collection game without too much going on under the hood. Little memory aspects and special powers add more than I want to remember for a game like this.

Außerdem bedienen sich alle Spieler am selben Pool, so dass man abschätzen kann, nach welchen Tieren man vielleicht gerade suchen sollte.  Tiefe 2/5 Viel Glück ist involviert. So strategisch, wie es in der Spielanleitung angepriesen ist, ist es leider nicht.  Spaßfaktor 1/5 Gewinner wird man fast eher "zufällig", weil man entweder das richtige Tier zieht oder die Gegner es nicht schaffen, das zu ziehen, was sie bräuc

[Rating: 4/10] Didn’t enjoy anything about it but there is nothing particularly annoying about the game either. Happy to never play again. Probably too much take that to play with round children. No depth to play with older. Unsure if there is an audience for this game.

[Rating: 4/10] Small collection game with nice cards. Lacks of real decisions and is therefore very luck based.

[Rating: 4/10] After 2 plays on BGA: A mediocre set-collection game with a heavy reliance on luck and simple rules. It didn’t do much for me. The card effects have a strong take-that feel, and there’s only limited room for meaningful tactical decisions.  When I lose, I’m left thinking: that felt unfair, there wasn’t much I could have done differently. When I win, it feels more like I got lucky than that I played particularly well. During other players’ turns, I often find myself thinking: this is a bit dull right now.  In short, it just never clicked for me. The illustration style is also a bit too childish
